summary: A Natura web article giving four tips for caring for white and salt-and-pepper hair, which is less rich in melanin, more dehydrated and brittle, and prone to yellowing. The tips cover purple or blue shampoo, intensive hydration with the Murumuru Ekos Care Mask, sun protection, and regular trims. The page is wrapped in heavy navigation and footer boilerplate, which is ignored here.
one_line: Natura's four-tip guide to keeping white and salt-and-pepper hair beautiful, shiny and free of yellowing.
key_facts: White and salt and pepper hair are described as extremely attractive and suitable for all skin types.
White hair is less rich in melanin, the natural pigment responsible for hair colour, so it is more dehydrated and rebellious.
According to Natura Brasil's hair expert Guilherme Cassolari, white hair turns yellow with time, so it should be cut frequently and kept well moisturised and tangle-free.
Tip #1 advises using a purple or blue shampoo, which contains pigments that eliminate the yellow tone and bring back shine.
Experts recommend a de-yellowing shampoo usually recommended for light blond hair to prevent white hair from turning yellow.
Tip #2 is 'hydration, hydration, hydration', because low melanin makes hair lose flexibility and become more brittle.
The article recommends the Murumuru Ekos Care Mask as a repairing treatment that penetrates the capillary fibre and reduces the hair's porosity.
Tip #3 advises staying out of the sun, since solar rays can compromise hair health and accentuate yellowing.
The article suggests wearing a hat or a scarf as sun protection, which also creates a glamorous, elegant look.
Tip #4 recommends a regular trim, since trimming the ends or opting for a short cut strengthens white hair.
Short hair needs less styling, which makes it easier to maintain and easier on the wallet.
The article notes that more and more women are giving up monthly colour touch-ups to hide natural grey or white hair.
